items.full_text_snippet: A new 10-meter resolution map shows which of the world's forests are natural, planted, or farmed, and how they are changing over time Protecting the planet's forests starts with a simple question: what type of forest are we looking at? From space, an old-growth rainforest, a eucalyptus plantation, and an oil palm estate can look like the same patch of green. But they hold very different amounts of carbon and biodiversity. Telling them apart, and knowing how each patch has changed over time, shows us where conservation is working and where natural forests are being converted into plantations and farms. Today, Google DeepMind and Google Research, together with the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), are releasing Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020 , a global map that categorizes every 10-by-10-meter patch of land on Earth into six distinct forest and land-use types, a key baseline for the EU's deforestation regulation. Alongside it, we're sharing an early time series that tracks how these forests changed each year from 2017 to 2025, including where natural forests were replaced by plantations or farms. For the first time, users can see at 10-meter detail worldwide, year by year, not just where forest was lost, but what replaced it: a timber plantation, a tree-crop farm or other land. Why "tree cover" isn't enough All forests store carbon and, together, forests are home to most of the world's land-based plant and animal species. But a forest’s ecological value also depends on its history: a primary forest that has never been cleared holds far more carbon and biodiversity than a single-species timber plantation that is harvested every decade or two. Most global maps only indicate whether trees are present. That's a challenge for those trying to protect natural forests. items.full_text_snippet: We're adding support for running GGUF models efficiently in transformers , so you can use checkpoints sized for your laptop's memory through the familiar transformers APIs. Pick a GGUF from the Hub, load it with from_pretrained , and start generating on your own machine. Running AI models on your laptop has become much easier, and llama.cpp has been a big part of that. Its inference engine powers local AI tools such as Ollama, LM Studio, and Jan. Alongside projects like MLX , it has helped make local inference a practical option for everyday use. A recent example of what local AI can feel like: GGUF , developed by the llama.cpp team, is a widely used format for local inference. The team also shares quantized checkpoints under ggml-org on the Hub . Publishers such as Unsloth , LM Studio Community , and bartowski also provide ready-to-use GGUF checkpoints in a range of quantizations, so users can pick the version that fits their machine. GGUF models have been downloaded millions of times. We want to make it easier to run these models locally with transformers, too. Compatibility is only useful if the model is pleasant to run. To bring performance close to llama.cpp, we're reusing its underlying ggml kernels through the kernels library, and reducing overhead in generate . Our initial focus is local inference on Apple Silicon, starting with the Qwen3.5 architecture. What is the GGUF file format? GGUF packages model weights and metadata, including tokenizer information and an optional chat template, in one file. It supports different quantization levels, letting you trade some precision for a smaller memory footprint. Variants such as Q4_K_M mix tensor precisions, using mostly 4-bit weights while keeping sensitive tensors at higher precision. items.summary: Training AI agents with reinforcement learning can be challenging because their tools, context, and decision-making are managed by complex frameworks. Agent Lightning connects existing agents to RL training, making it easier to improve them without rebuilding them. The post Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses appeared first on Microsoft Research .
items.full_text_snippet: At a glance Harnessed Agentic RL: Microsoft Research Asia introduces a training paradigm in which the same agent harness used in deployment participates directly in reinforcement learning, removing the need to reimplement the agent inside the training framework. Lightweight by design: Agent Lightning v1.0 delivers a complete agent RL control plane in roughly 3,500 lines of code. Native Kubernetes support: agents run as standard Kubernetes jobs on self-managed clusters, cloud Kubernetes, or local infrastructure, with no dependency on paid commercial sandbox services. Data-efficient training recipe: an end-to-end coding agent pipeline raised Qwen3.5-9B from 41.8% to 56.4% Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, a 14.6 percentage point gain, using only about 6,000 training samples based on open sourced dataset. AI agents have evolved from single models to complex full-stack systems built from models, tools, and execution environments. Their capabilities increasingly depend on the agent harness that coordinates them from outside the model. Reinforcement learning (RL) is an approach where AI systems learn through trial and error, guided by rewards and penalties for their actions. RL can make those agents better, but most agent RL systems require developers to reimplement the agent inside the training framework. That is costly, and it means the agent being trained is not quite the agent that gets deployed. To address this, researchers at Microsoft Research Asia have introduced the Harnessed Agentic RL training paradigm and open-sourced a fully rebuilt Agent Lightning v1.0 (opens in new tab) . Compared with the original, Agent Lightning, v1.0 puts more emphasis on staying lightweight, on integrating with real harnesses, and on a complete, reproducible agent RL training pipeline. items.full_text_snippet: OpenAI made its Decisions API model widely available to users for the first time, entering the market for fast, cheap intelligence that recently made TypeSafe, a startup founded by a former researcher at the frontier lab, a $7.6 billion company . TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost. Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost. “The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said. “In the future, we may sort of like have specific training to make our models like even better in these ways. But right now, it’s just plain old Luna that gets the job done.” Announced at the company’s developer day on September 29, the Decisions API became available to all customers on Thursday. OpenAI added new voice and visual modalities to the public version, and worked to ensure lower latency in regions around the world by targeting its inference resources geographically. In initial trials with customers like Box, Datadog, Ramp, and Speak, engineers used the API to replace OpenAI’s LLMs with higher throughput. items.full_text_snippet: The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation . PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites . It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress. The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app. Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12. So how did two such ubiquitous, decades-old flaws that affect nearly every website on the internet suddenly come to light? AI, naturally, particularly via OpenAI and Google’s Wiz. Security testing company Calif was engaged in OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative to find flaws in open source software. Using GPT‑5.6 Sol, it found one of the flaws, OpenAI disclosed in a blog post . Separately, the Wiz team also used AI, namely its Wiz Atlas security AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol to find multiple vulnerabilities in PHP. Both OpenAI and Wiz followed responsible security research practices and worked with PHP on patches before publicly disclosing the flaws. Then they all worked together to flesh out what they found, and test the patches, drawing in a host of others to help. items.full_text_snippet: Games are one of the most creative forms of expression, and the gaming community keeps growing. But game creation has historically been limited to a select group of people who have technical experience and knowledge of complex game engines. Today, we’re introducing Playground, an experimental gaming platform that lets you create, play, and share custom games. Playground lowers the barriers to creation, so bringing game ideas to life can now be as easy as describing it through a few prompts — no coding experience required. Create your custom game With Playground’s conversational interface, you can direct the game just by typing what you want to build. Start from a blank canvas, remix starter prompts, or use guided support to shape your concept — and then test it right away. Want to tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment? Just ask. Alongside OlmoEarth v1.3, we’re sharing precomputed, annual embeddings for the whole planet (10m, 64- and 128-dimensions), plus a new browser-based tool to explore and customize maps based on those embeddings — the OlmoEarth Embeddings Explorer . This means anyone can put  OlmoEarth v1.3 to work right away, from tracking change over time to finding similar places—no sign-in, and no advanced technical knowledge required. Until now, the primary way to use OlmoEarth was fine-tuning in OlmoEarth Studio: training a model for each task and running it over satellite imagery to make a map. That requires GPU access and the ability to download and store the imagery . Embedding models compress satellite data into ready-to-use features that can be reused cheaply for many tasks. With OlmoEarth v1.3, we’re excited to give users more ways to explore and engage with planetary artifacts in whatever way suits them best. Compute once, reuse everywhere An embedding represents what the model learned from millions of images. OlmoEarth v1.3 reads a year of radar (Sentinel-1) and multispectral (Sentinel-2 and Landsat) satellite time series and produces one 128-dimensional vector for every 10-meter pixel on Earth; the first 64 dimensions also work on their own as a smaller embedding. Foundation models and global embeddings are expensive to produce, and to make sure everyone is able to access the benefits, we’ve computed these embeddings for the entire planet and shared them with the community on Source Cooperative . From there, a crop map, a land-cover map, or a change analysis becomes a lightweight modeling problem: train a small classifier on top and run it locally. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 19 Oct 2026] Title: VHDLBench: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for VHDL-Based Chip Design View a PDF of the paper titled VHDLBench: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for VHDL-Based Chip Design, by Patrik Drazic and 2 other authors View PDF Abstract: The rapid evolution of digital circuit complexity demands innovative approaches to hardware design automation. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have influenced software development, their application to Hardware Description Language (HDL) generation remains largely unexplored, particularly for VHDL. This paper presents a comprehensive study for AI-assisted digital circuit design, addressing gaps in current Electronic Design Automation workflows. The work introduces a VHDL dataset of 18,500+ syntax-verified examples from open-source repositories and converted Verilog designs. Five 7B-parameter LLMs were fine-tuned using parameter-efficient QLoRA technique, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. To evaluate model efficacy, a rigorous three-level pipeline was established: (1) syntax and synthesis validation, (2) functional simulation with testbenches, and (3) FPGA prototyping on Zynq SoCs. Results show fine-tuned models achieve up to 92% syntax correctness and 73% functional accuracy on common design tasks, with DeepSeek-Coder demonstrating the highest performance gains. Generated designs were successfully deployed on real hardware, confirming not only syntactic but operational viability. This work demonstrates that LLMs, when tailored with domain-specific data and lightweight fine-tuning can contribute meaningfully to the future of generative EDA workflows. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 21 Oct 2026] Title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting View a PDF of the paper titled Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting, by Nurul Labib Sayeedi and 4 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Many NP-complete (NPC) problems have a polynomial-time (P) twin that differs in a single structural detail, such as 3- versus 2-colouring a graph. A model that reasons rather than recalls should notice which side of this boundary a problem falls on, yet existing benchmarks either fix the wording of each task or ignore its complexity class, so they cannot separate the two. We introduce P2NPCBench, a benchmark of 12 problem families in which every NPC problem is paired with a P twin posed over the same surface. To remove the textbook cues that enable recall, we build it with AgentGAN, an adversarial multi-agent framework in which a generator rewrites each statement until a panel of frozen code models fails, while an executable validity gate keeps every rewrite answer- and class-preserving. The result is 2,114 hardened statements with hand-verified reference human solvers. Evaluating 12 proprietary and open-source models, we find that every model scores lower on NPC statements than on their P twins (35.4% vs. 63.8% pass@1), and that 95.1% of model-family pairs fail more often on the NPC side. A tenfold time limit raises NPC accuracy only from 28.5% to 31.9%, so failures stem from wrong or crashing programs rather than slow ones. Hardening also narrows the class gap from 24.8 to 14.6 points, showing that part of the apparent gap reflects familiarity with textbook phrasing rather than complexity class. 2026-10-22 15:11:14 来源： 量子位 中电信人工智能科技有限公司星辰通用人工智能实验室正式发布并开源意图理解专用模型 Xing4.0-29B-Intent 中国电信人工智能科技有限公司星辰通用人工智能实验室正式发布并开源意图理解专用模型 Xing4.0-29B-Intent，同步开放275万条训练语料、模型权重与推理镜像。模型将意图识别与参数抽取结合起来，把用户的一句话转换为业务系统可以继续处理的结构化信息。 目前，Xing4.0-29B-Intent模型能力已在电信万号客服、智能家居音箱等终端产品中开始应用，服务于对话意图识别、工单智能路由和口语指令解析。此次开源将为更多开发者提供模型及配套资源，支持接入各自的业务场景。 01判断题还是填空题 “帮我把卧室的灯调成暖黄。”一句日常的设备操作指令，既包含用户想做的事，也包含完成操作所需的具体信息。系统需要从自然表达中提取这些信息，才能交给后续应用处理。 面对这句话，仅判断出“控制灯光”还不够。系统还需要知道：哪个房间？卧室；什么设备？灯；调成什么状态？暖黄。 Jev类决策模型主要“做选择题”，返回类型化决策，从给定的候选中挑选答案；参数抽取相当于“做填空题”，提取完成任务所需的具体信息。Xing4.0-29B-Intent同时支持这两类任务，也支持一句话包含多个意图、多个参数和多个实体的情况。 模型采用统一模式驱动语义解析框架（USP，Unified Schema-driven Semantic Parsing），以“类别＋参数”的层级结构组织结果，按照预先定义的字段规则输出JSON格式信息。异构任务目标如：意图理解、实体识别、关系抽取、事件抽取等任务统一采用统一套输入输出格式约束，便于下游任务快速接入，稳定解析，迁移成本极低。 02为什么不直接用通用大模型？ 看到这里你可能会问：通用大模型不是已经“无所不能”了吗，为什么还要专门的意图理解模型？ 因为在这类场景里，通用大模型有三个“先天短板”。 第一，输出速度 通用大模型习惯“想清楚再回答”，动辄数百上千字的长篇推理，对于“工单转给谁”这样的问题，等它说完，客户早就挂电话了。Xing4.0-29B-Intent只对任务处理所需的关键决策信息做出快速响应，没有长篇推理，平均输出几十个token，完整结果响应时延可以做到百毫秒级。 第二，决策成本 动用通用大模型去做分类和信息提取，无异于杀鸡用牛刀。意图理解模型规模小、调用省，当一个场景每天要调用上百万次时，成本差距会成倍放大。 第三，决策可靠性 通用大模型的输出是自由文本，同一个问题可能得到十种说法，下游系统难以稳定解析。意图理解模型的输出被严格约束在预定义的结构里：字段确定、格式可校验，不给“自由发挥”留空间。 一句话总结：在响应及时度要求高、场景相对收敛、决策执行相对明确的地方，意图理解模型是比通用大模型更快、更便宜、更可靠的选择。 这条赛道已经有先行者。以Jev为代表的轻量级决策模型推出后，迅速成为开发者社区热议的焦点。市场的反响印证了一个判断：意图理解不必依赖大模型“强推理”，专用小模型同样可以做到又快又准。 03效果说话 两组评测检验识别与抽取能力 模型能否读懂用户多意图细粒度的需求，可以从两个层面检验：一是既判断对类别，又提取对具体内容；二是只看类别判断，能否做到不漏选、不多选。技术团队据此开展了两组评测，分别考察完整抽取结果和类别判断能力。 第一组 不仅类别要对 具体内容也要对 第一组评测从48个中英文公开数据集中按比例抽取6000道题，覆盖意图理解、实体识别、关系抽取和事件抽取四类任务。它考察的不只是“分到哪一类”，还包括“具体提取出了什么”。 以前文的灯光指令为例，仅判断出“控制灯光”还不够，还要提取出“卧室”“灯”“暖黄”等信息。这个例子用于说明评分要求：类别正确但内容缺失或错误，不能算作完整正确的抽取结果。 items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 生数科技Motubrain团队将直播Physical AI训练全流程，持续半个月 量子位的朋友们 2026-10-21 17:45:22 来源： 量子位 10月21日，生数科技世界模型团队正式开启Motubrain 2.0训练全流程公开直播 大模型训练过程，开始更多地出现在公众视野中。 此前，小米MiMo负责人罗福莉公开了MiMo-V2.6强化学习阶段的训练进展，让外界看到了大模型训练中的一些具体细节。 现在，Physical AI领域也有了类似尝试。 10月21日，生数科技世界模型团队正式开启Motubrain 2.0训练全流程公开直播，计划持续半个月，向公众展示具身模型的训练过程及研究进展。 这次直播关注一个问题：Physical AI究竟如何实现？ Physical AI，即物理人工智能，希望让AI能够理解物理环境，并通过机器人完成实际任务。相比大语言模型，Physical AI 还需要解决动作决策、任务执行和跨场景泛化等问题。 Motubrain 系列是生数科技研发的具身模型，致力于为机器人构建具备通用能力的“大脑”，探索不同任务、场景和机器人本体之间的能力泛化。 Motubrain 2.0即将开源。在正式开源前，团队选择率先公开其训练全流程，向外界展示这款模型从训练、测试到能力迭代的过程。 此次公开训练涵盖四个环节： 1、预训练：观察训练规模对模型性能及零样本泛化能力的影响。 2、后训练：针对具体任务进一步训练，提升任务执行能力。 3、Agent任务执行：探索模型能否将已有经验迁移到其他任务。 4、RSI（递归自我改进）探索：研究模型能否根据执行反馈评估并改进自身行动。 此次直播的特别之处，是尝试打开具身模型训练的“黑盒”。 过去，外界了解具身智能技术进展，主要通过机器人Demo、评测结果和论文。模型经历了怎样的训练、不同阶段的能力如何变化，通常很难直接观察。 Motubrain 2.0 选择公开从训练、测试到能力迭代的全过程，希望让外界看到模型如何逐步形成能力，也能看到训练中的失败、试错和调整。 对于具身智能行业而言，这种方式让模型研发过程更加透明。研究者和开发者不仅能看到最终结果，也有机会了解训练中遇到的具体问题，以及团队如何通过实验和反馈不断改进模型。 同时，团队也希望借助此次直播，与技术同行分享研究中的经验、问题和思考，共同探讨规模化训练、跨任务泛化和自主改进等关键问题，为Physical AI实现范式的探索提供更多参考。 当然，相关研究仍处于探索阶段，具体效果还需要后续实验和评测验证。相比只展示机器人最终能做什么，公开模型如何训练、能力如何形成，同样具有研究价值。 直播入口：www.motubrain.com/motubrain2.0-live 官网链接：www.motubrain.com 本文由生数科技提供，量子位获授权转载，观点归原作者所有。 版权所有，未经授权不得以任何形式转载及使用，违者必究。

items.full_text_snippet: Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up. Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials. The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents , accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand. 1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. The company says it is working with other companies to expand the service. “Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time,” the company said in a blog post . “1Password for Agents gives people a trusted way to delegate tasks to personal AI agents while keeping control of the passwords, secrets, and credentials those tasks require.” Online agentic activity has increasingly unsettled major institutions. Indeed, 1Password’s new platform is launching on the same day that Axios reports that U.S. banks have begun to detect agentic activity inside user accounts. items.full_text_snippet: Design platform Canva released its first image generation model, called Canva Craft, developed by its research team to compete with same-category models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta. The company said its model works in two stages. In the first stage, it interprets users’ prompts and creates a plan with details like spatial relationships of elements, relative scale, visual hierarchy, and information for text generation. In the second stage, its model generates an image of up to 2K resolution in a possible 30 different aspect ratios for various platforms. Canva said that this approach allows it to create images with accurate details of objects and legible text. Plus, users would be able to make precise edits without changing other parts of the image. The company noted that rather than using photographs, it used designs to train this model using human-designed templates from Canva’s library, including posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-rich layouts. That means images generated with Canva Craft could be converted into layered designs using Canva Magic, the company’s image-to-design transformer. Last year, the platform released its own model that understands designs and layers . Canva Craft is available on the company’s platform to all users, who can access the model from the Dream Lab tab. The model will also be available through the Canva API. Plus, the company plans to support image generation in third-party chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini through Canva’s MCP. Canva has used a bunch of image models for generation in its platform, so it’s likely that the new models will help save API costs for the company. It said that besides costs, the new model also allows the platform to have better quality and speed control. In 2024, Canva acquired media generation platform Leonardo.ai . items.summary: Microsoft’s new AI diagnostic system beat generalist doctors on hard cases, according to a study in Science. But most of the improvement seems to come from the AI models underneath, not from Microsoft’s system itself.
items.full_text_snippet: Microsoft’s AI diagnostic system correctly diagnosed complex medical cases in a simulation more than twice as often as generalist physicians, according to a study published Thursday in Science. Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft AI’s CEO, called the result a step toward “medical superintelligence.” The system, dubbed MAI-DxO (DxO for short), coordinates several AI agents that act like a panel of doctors. They question a patient, order tests, and debate a diagnosis. In a simulation using complex cases from the New England Journal of Medicine, it was correct 83% of the time. Primary care doctors and general internists, working individually with reference materials, were correct 36% of the time. One note: Cases this complex are usually handled by specialists or physician teams, who weren’t part of the comparison. “There is something very substantial and exciting here,” Dominic King, vice president of Health at Microsoft AI, told TechCrunch. “The biggest challenge in healthcare delivery at the moment is the growing mismatch between demand and supply of medical expertise.” In publishing these results , Microsoft joins Go o gle and OpenAI in claiming that its AI can match or outperform doctors. The study’s own data suggests that much of the improvement comes from more powerful underlying AI models, with Microsoft’s orchestration system adding gains on top. Microsoft tested MAI-DxO with models from several companies, including OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, and DeepSeek, but its best results came with OpenAI’s GPT-5 and GPT-5.5. items.full_text_snippet: Uber and OpenAI announced an expansion of their partnership on Thursday, with the ride-share giant telling TechCrunch that its entire global workforce — some 30,000 people — will now be using ChatGPT Work. ChatGPT Work was introduced in July as an enterprise-focused AI agent that corporate teams could deploy for various workflows. Uber originally piloted ChatGPT Work with 1,000 employees earlier this year but has now scaled up its usage to the entire company. That earlier pilot was deployed to workers from across Uber’s various departments, including finance, operations, and product. Indeed, a majority of the early adopters — some 80% — were non-engineers, Sumanth Sukumar, Uber’s VP of engineering, told TechCrunch. “They used it for a wide range of tasks: analyzing complex data from our operations to identify trends and develop recommendations; localizing training materials for different markets and languages; and building personalized interactive dashboards to manage their daily work,” he said. Yet while the ride-share giant is now going all in on ChatGPT, it has not settled on exactly how employees will use it. “Our approach is to make powerful AI tools available across Uber while giving teams room to experiment,” Sukumar said. “For example, earlier this year we paired 30 AI engineers with teams across Uber and gave them two weeks to automate key parts of their job. Those ‘AI pods’ showed us how much opportunity there is when you combine technical expertise with a deep understanding of a particular job.” Uber didn’t disclose how much it’s spending on the new rollout of the chatbot. Instead, Sukumar said the company will track how employees use the tool. “We’ll look at how employees are using the technology, the kinds of workflows they develop and how it helps them work more effectively. items.full_text_snippet: Spotify had a strong third quarter , reaching 788 million monthly active users and generating nearly €5 billion (around $5.6 billion USD) in revenue. But the more interesting takeaway from its earnings call was how the company sees people listening to music in the future, and why the rise of AI agents could be good news for its business. Co-CEO Gustav Söderström thinks the music streaming giant is particularly well-suited to this shift. “Spotify is in one of the few categories that actually stands to thrive in the agentic age,” Söderström tells investors. “This is because agents excel at replacing and taking care of things people would rather not do. People love getting rid of chores. But entertainment is the opposite. Nobody asks an agent to ‘summarize a song’ for them.” Instead of opening Spotify, searching for an artist, and building a playlist themselves, listeners could ask an AI assistant to do the work for them. They might want music for a run, a podcast about something they’ve been discussing with an AI, or an audiobook recap that picks up exactly where they left off. Spotify wants to be the service those agents turn to, letting people discover music and interact with Spotify through conversations rather than just its own app. Notably, Spotify was the first music service to integrate with Meta’s Muse assistant , and it also integrates with ChatGPT and Claude. “Our goal is to be the media service that you use from any agent, really turning the growth of agents into a tailwind rather than a headwind. That is exactly what we are seeing now. We are seeing really good adoption of Spotify inside these agents. While other companies are maybe trying to figure out what to do and many are leaning out, we are actually leaning in and participating in the growth instead of standing by the roadside and looking at it,” said Söderström. items.summary: MIT introduces SEAL, a framework enabling large language models to self-edit and update their weights via reinforcement learning. The post MIT Researchers Unveil “SEAL”: A New Step Towards Self-Improving AI first appeared on Synced .
items.full_text_snippet: The concept of AI self-improvement has been a hot topic in recent research circles, with a flurry of papers emerging and prominent figures like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman weighing in on the future of self-evolving intelligent systems. Now, a new paper from MIT, titled “Self-Adapting Language Models,” introduces SEAL (Self-Adapting LLMs) , a novel framework that allows large language models (LLMs) to update their own weights. This development is seen as another significant step towards the realization of truly self-evolving AI. The research paper, published yesterday, has already ignited considerable discussion, including on Hacker News. SEAL proposes a method where an LLM can generate its own training data through “self-editing” and subsequently update its weights based on new inputs. Crucially, this self-editing process is learned via reinforcement learning, with the reward mechanism tied to the updated model’s downstream performance. The timing of this paper is particularly notable given the recent surge in interest surrounding AI self-evolution. Earlier this month, several other research efforts garnered attention, including Sakana AI and the University of British Columbia’s “Darwin-Gödel Machine (DGM),” CMU’s “Self-Rewarding Training (SRT),” Shanghai Jiao Tong University’s “MM-UPT” framework for continuous self-improvement in multimodal large models, and the “UI-Genie” self-improvement framework from The Chinese University of Hong Kong in collaboration with vivo. Adding to the buzz, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman recently shared his vision of a future with self-improving AI and robots in his blog post, “The Gentle Singularity.” He posited that while the initial millions of humanoid robots would need traditional manufacturing, they would then be able to “operate the entire supply chain to build more robots, which can in turn build more chip fabrication facilities, data centers, and so on.” This was quickly followed by a tweet from @VraserX, claiming an OpenAI insider reveal...

items.full_text_snippet:
Stops Claude Code from spending your five-hour usage window in ten minutes. agent-usage-guard is a Claude Code mod : it runs inside Claude Code and holds runaway spend before it happens. It reads your plan's live usage, and it holds subagent fan-out, heavy-context churn and retry loops. Recorded from Claude Code's interactive UI with the guard loaded. A scripted local API stands in for Claude, so the sessions and token counts are staged and no usage is spent. Every question on screen is the guard's own. Rebuild it from the Northstar fixture . It acts before the spend, not after it: before an agent starts, a prompt is sent, or a tool call runs. Agent limits hold across every Claude Code session on your machine, and fan-out and heavy context are capped at any usage level, not only near the limit. When you are at the keyboard it asks you, in Claude Code's own question dialog. When nobody can answer, it refuses and tells Claude why, so the model can wait, batch the work, or stop. /agent-guard report shows what it did. Plan-aware. It reads the 5-hour and weekly percentages Claude Code reports, and keeps the end of the window for you. One answer covers a while. items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 实探宁德时代总部：“去宁化”是喊太大声了 杰西卡 2026-10-21 12:35:56 来源： 量子位 杰西卡 发自 ROBO-车 量子位ROBO | 公众号 AI4ROBO 一块电池，搅动了汽车产业链风云。 理想斥资26.5亿元入股欣旺达动力，小米联合中创新航等企业开发电池……一场围绕动力电池核心技术、成本和供应链话语权的讨论，最近愈演愈烈。 就连宁德时代也亲自下场回应： 会造车，不一定会造电池。还是要专业的人，做专业的事。 然而在这场风波中，上汽旗下智己却反其道而行之，宣布即将推出的LS8 NEO纯电，将 全系搭载宁德时代电池 。 不仅如此，智己还联合宁德时代，邀请媒体前往宁德参观工厂——也包括量子位ROBO。 有点意思。 车圈目前似乎分开了两波阵营。一边是车企开始寻求降低对供应链的依赖；另一边在主动把和宁德时代的合作推至台前。 智己为什么坚持合作宁德时代？宁德时代的电芯、电池包和车企自研电池有什么不同？双方又是怎样看待当下趋势的？ 带着这些疑问，我决定前往福建宁德，现场看看。 走进宁德时代，原来一颗电芯是这样成型的 十月的宁德，绿水青山，桂花飘香，路边还能看到蜻蜓飞来飞去。不了解的人或许很难想象，在这片山水之间，坐落着全球最大的动力电池企业。 这里是宁德时代总部。 其实参观前，我预想到这次行程会比较严格，但没想到这么严格。拍摄设备的序列号要提前报备，抵达宁德时代科技大楼后，需要先去访客中心登记、领取访客卡，再刷卡进入。 科技大楼据说借鉴了 方形电芯 的造型设计，内部能够容纳5000多人办公。 大厅里还有一个展厅，我们待了一个上午，陆续遇到好几批前来参观的访客。 展厅门口就是一座园区布局图。 以湖泊为界，宁德时代的办公、研发和生产设施分布在不同区域。据讲解员介绍，仅在宁德当地，公司就有 超过5万名员工 ，全球员工总数超过23万人。 这家2011年成立的企业，从2017年开始连续多年位居全球动力电池装车量榜首，2025年的全球市场份额达到39.2%——相当于 全球每卖出三辆电动汽车 ，大约就有一辆搭载宁德时代电池。 十几年间，宁德时代的业务也从 动力电池 延伸到 储能、换电、船舶 等领域。 展厅里陈列的是宁德时代一路布局的各种形态的电池，从磷酸铁锂、三元锂，到钠离子、凝聚态电池，有的 已经量产 ，有的还处在 研发验证 阶段。 其中一个低温展示装置挺有意思。钠离子电池被装在一个透明的低温装置里，温度已经降到 零下30多摄氏度 ，电池旁结了厚冰，罩壁上还有遇冷凝结的水雾。 讲解员介绍，相比传统锂离子电池，钠离子电池在低温性能方面的优势更明显，宁德时代也在探索将钠离子与其他电池体系组合，以改善车辆在寒冷地区的使用表现。 展厅也集中摆放了一部分面向不同场景的电芯产品，拿在手里大部分都比较有分量。 即便是这个最轻薄的凝聚态电池（能量密度高达500瓦时/千克），也比看起来要沉不少。 宁德时代还展示了研发中心做的一些测试，包括高压冲水、冲击、跌落、火烧、浸水、震动方面的测试。 以浸水测试为例，宁德时代通常会把电池包放在水池里，浸泡半个小时、24小时、48小时不等。浸泡完成后，要确保没有任何一滴水珠渗透到电池包内部才算合格。 当然了，模型展示终究还是纸上谈兵。一颗电芯究竟怎么制造，还得去工厂看看。 还有一个细节是，我发现工作人员的着装也有所不同。据讲解员透露，电芯制造涉及不同的环境控制要求，需要对湿度、静电和微小粉尘等等因素进行管理。 看来不管是对外对内都是一样的严谨。 参观过程中，还有方壳电芯的展示样品让我们近距离接触。方方扁扁的，像个放大版的磁带。 这就是新能源汽车动力电池最基本的组成单元之一。 一颗电芯内部包含正负极材料、隔膜、电解液等，经过材料加工、装配和检测，最终形成能够独立充放电的单元。而一辆纯电动车的电池包，往往需要 数十颗乃至上百颗电芯 共同工作。 因此，电池厂需要考虑的，除了单颗电芯的性能，还有不同电芯之间的 一致性 。 items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 7 Oct 2026] Title: Revisiting Explainable AI through Model-Independent Concept Dictionaries View a PDF of the paper titled Revisiting Explainable AI through Model-Independent Concept Dictionaries, by Thomas Schnake and 5 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Modern applications of AI rely on increasingly complex models. Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a set of techniques aimed at improving model transparency. However, existing XAI methods typically assume input features to be inherently interpretable, or they rely on intermediate internal abstractions that are difficult to characterize and highly architecture-specific, hindering consistent use across models. To address these limitations, we propose DictXAI, a method that defines concepts directly in the input domain via a dictionary---a large, potentially overcomplete set of predefined elements, each carrying an interpretable meaning. Technically, DictXAI first computes a sparse code of the input and then attributes the model's prediction to the associated dictionary elements. We demonstrate the actionable nature of DictXAI explanations, showing that they can attribute AI malfunctions (e.g., Clever Hans effects) directly to identifiable artifact patterns in the data, while fostering human-AI alignment on intricate biomedical signals. We further demonstrate our method's ability to operate across a wide variety of dictionaries, including learned image bases, analytically defined waveforms for electrocardiography, and experimentally acquired dictionary elements. Overall, our results show that DictXAI provides more interpretable, actionable, and architecture-agnostic insights than classical XAI or existing concept-based approaches. To be useful in practice, such an explanation should change few features and change them as little as possible, properties known as sparsity and proximity. We observe that existing methods remain limited in this respect, especially for numerical features, whether they are model-agnostic and amortised, or gradient-based with full access to the model. In this paper, we propose FlowCF, a model-agnostic generative method that frames CF generation as sparse transport from the factual to the target class. We solve this transport with flow matching, which we extend to mixed feature types with a novel mixed flow operator, and exploit the resulting geometry to optimise for sparsity through a gating network that minimises the number of features the transport changes. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets demonstrate that FlowCF produces the best numerical sparsity and proximity, changing 29% of the numerical features where the best baseline changes 89%, at 70% smaller displacement, while remaining comparable on the other desiderata. Important New in OpenShell 0.1.x: a stable release cadence, new isolation primitives, an expanded extension surface, and new APIs. Read the 0.1.0 upgrade guide . OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials. OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network. You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it. OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied. Kernel-level enforcement. Each agent runs in an isolated sandbox. Kernel controls confine which files it can access and which system calls it can make, and every network connection passes through a policy check before it leaves the sandbox. Agents never see real credentials; OpenShell adds them only to requests bound for approved endpoints. Formally verified policy changes. Before a policy change is approved, OpenShell uses formal verification to flag risky new access it would grant, such as reaching a new host with credentials or calling a new API method, so those changes wait for human review. items.full_text_snippet: The bad week for cybersecurity just got worse for thousands more companies, who were spied on by Chinese hackers following the breach of IT management and remote access giant ConnectWise. Security researchers at Microsoft say the China state-aligned hackers broke into ConnectWise’s cloud backup service and stole application credentials that are used to establish data links between ConnectWise and its corporate customers, who rely on the cloud service to back up their company’s data. By stealing the credentials, the hackers could log in to the customer’s Microsoft-hosted environment as if they were an authorized user and access their emails and other files. According to Microsoft, the hackers used AI agents to rapidly hack into around 2,250 organizations at a rate of almost 3,000 attempted sign-ins per minute. Microsoft said this speed gives defenders “little time to detect and respond.” The speed of the mass-hacks was attributed to the use of AI agents, specifically ARTEX, an open source AI framework that works with AI models to stress-test cyber defenses. The same AI software was used in a recent compromise of South Korea’s financial systems, many of which had weak security and lacked multi-factor authentication. ConnectWise said it’s paused access to its cloud backup system and is investigating the breach. As of Thursday, the company said it was working on restoring the service.

items.full_text_snippet: Ok, this one is really best explained with a visualiser: NetHack’s level generation has a lot of interesting things, but I wanted to focus on the Gnomish Mines because of their use of Cellular Automata. This gives it an organic caves feel, while the majority of the game is spent in square rooms. It’s very straightforward: Randomly pick 40% of the cells to be floor Apply four passes of Cellular Automata Fix up disconnected caves with extra corridors Let’s dive into the cellular automata specifically. There’s only two states – floor or rock. And each pass works by counting how many floor tiles are in the 8-neighbor hood of each cell. Pass 1: 0-2 → rock; 3-4 → unchanged, 5-8 → floor Pass 2: 0-4 → unchanged; 5 → rock;  6-8 → unchanged Pass 3: 0-2 → rock; 3-8 → unchanged. Pass 4: same as pass 3 Interestingly, pass 1 is unbuffered. Each cell is updated in place before moving to the next cell. All the rest are buffered – all cells have new computed values, then the entire grid updated at once. Pass 1 creates floors near other floors, and creates rocks near other rocks. I’d call this a “clustering” pass, that pushes the random tiles towards wide open areas of tiles. The unbuffering is important here so that you don’t flop-flop, turning something rock→floor near something turning floor→rock. Passes 3 and 4 are erosion routines, it’s a very common use of cellular automata. If you have 6-8 rocks nearby, then you also become a rock. That tends to smooth out corners, and delete tiny islands. Pass 2 though… It turns cells to rock if they have exactly 5 floor neighbors (i.e. 3 rock neighbors). I’m still struggling to understand what purpose this is intended to achieve. Any ideas?

In announcing the round, Blacksmith co-founder and CEO Aditya Jayaprakash said the company was founded to make continuous integration (CI) — the process of building, testing, merging, and validating code changes — “less painful.” In a blog post, he said that “most companies are struggling to keep up with the volume of CI they need to run,” especially in an era where so much code is written by AI. “As agents write more of the world’s software, the question that matters is whether it can be trusted,” he added. The company also announced that its annual recurring revenue has grown 17x and that it has run over 90 million CI jobs, or individual automated code checks. Customers include Mercury and Granola. The Series C comes just two months after its $45 million Series B, which valued the company at $550 million. A year ago, Blacksmith was valued at $60 million after raising a $10 million Series A. It has raised $125 million to date.

projects.readme_excerpt:
Download from [Releases](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee/releases/latest).

- **Windows 10/11**: run `Filee-<version>-win-Setup.exe`, or unzip the `win-Portable.zip` and run `Filee.exe`.
  Setup is Filee's own installer, in Filee's languages, and needs nothing else on the PC. It can add the Explorer
  menu, start at sign-in, the `filee` command and optional engines; silent installs take Inno Setup's switches
  (`/VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES`).
- **macOS 13+** (preview): unpack the `osx-arm64` or `osx-x64` package and run `./install.sh`.
  The build isn't notarized yet, so allow the first start in System Settings → Privacy & Security → **Open Anyway**.
- **Linux x64/ARM64** (Ubuntu 22.04+): unpack the package and run `./install.sh` (no root, needs Python 3).
  Drag gestures need X11. On Wayland, use the drop zone and the file manager's right-click menu.

Filee shows new releases in its menu and updates itself, keeping your settings and engines. After an update, a few
slides show what's new.
